newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ruling coalition defers oil price decision.
newsitem.headline: India's ruling coalition defers oil price decision.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition on Monday deferred a decision on whether to raise petroleum product prices and scheduled another meeting for June 27, a senior alliance member said.

Railways Minister Ram Vilas Paswan told reporters after the 2-1/2-hour meeting of the centre-left alliance's Steering Committee that the issue of the mounting oil subsidy bill had been put off until the June 27 meeting.
Information Minister Jaipal Reddy, who is the United Front's spokesman, said there was some discussion of the issue of oil prices. "But the discussion was inconclusive," he said.

The leftwing parties in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition have steadfastly opposed raising the prices of some petroleum products such as kerosene and diesel to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies.

The government owed domestic oil firms 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March to compensate them for selling some petroleum products below world market levels. Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has said some prices might have to be raised to rein in the cost to the government.
